nodes.name: X-ray inspection for advanced packaging (2.5D/3D solder defects)
nodes.description: Volumetric X-ray inspection systems (CT, laminography) for detecting voids, cracks, missing bumps, head-in-pillow defects, and bond-line thickness variation in micro-bumps, hybrid-bonded interfaces, and solder-joint arrays in 2.5D/3D chiplet packages. Sub-1µm resolution critical for HBM stack qualification. Bottleneck: limited vendor population (Comet Yxlon, Camtek, Onto Innovation, KLA) and 12-18 month lead times for system delivery.

metrics.name: System delivery lead time
metrics.description: Typical lead time from order to installation for advanced X-ray inspection systems; sourced from Comet Yxlon and Camtek product literature.

metrics.name: Top-2 vendor market share (Comet Yxlon + Camtek)
metrics.description: Combined market share of leading vendors in advanced packaging X-ray inspection; Onto Innovation and KLA serve broader metrology markets. Source: 2025 analyst reports on semiconductor metrology equipment market.

metrics.name: Resolution (X-ray imaging)
metrics.description: State-of-the-art sub-micron resolution achieved by Comet Yxlon CA20 and Onto Innovation Dragonfly; required for sub-0.5µm defect detection in fine-pitch interconnects.

nodes.notes: X-ray inspection is a critical post-assembly process control step. Market is concentrated: Comet Yxlon leads with CA20 system; Camtek (Eagle family) and Onto Innovation (Dragonfly) serve HBM/2.5D; KLA provides broader metrology but focuses on wafer-fab metrology. Lead time of 12-18 months for custom system commissioning is a secondary constraint on fab ramp capacity. No shortage episodes documented in 2024-2025, but systems are ordered 18+ months ahead for major OSAT capacity buildouts.

nodes.name: Optical metrology and bump inspection (2D/3D surface topology, height, coplanarity)
nodes.description: High-resolution automated optical inspection (AOI) and laser-triangulation systems for measuring bump height, coplanarity, surface defects, and 3D topology on flip-chip dies and micro-bumps prior to underfill and reflow. Nanometer-scale vertical resolution (0.5-5nm) required for solder-joint reliability. AI-driven defect classification for high-throughput production yield monitoring. Vendors: Camtek, Confovis, Onto Innovation (Dragonfly 2D). Lower cost alternative to X-ray for high-volume process control.

metrics.name: Vertical resolution
metrics.description: Best-in-class optical metrology systems achieve <1nm vertical measurement repeatability; Confovis WAFERinspect and Camtek Eagle G5 meet this specification.

metrics.name: Top-3 vendor presence
metrics.description: Camtek (Eagle family), Confovis (WAFERinspect), Onto Innovation (Dragonfly 2D) dominate optical metrology for chiplet assembly; KLA also supplies optical tools.

metrics.name: Throughput (typical AOI system)
metrics.description: High-speed optical metrology systems can process 6-10 wafers/hour depending on die size and sampling strategy; critical for cycle-time management in OSAT lines.

nodes.notes: Optical metrology is less capital-intensive than X-ray and more suitable for 100%-sampling process control in high-volume production. Camtek is the market leader in advanced packaging AOI; Confovis is a specialist focused on 3DIC and chiplet applications (Jena, Germany). Onto Innovation's Dragonfly 2D complements their X-ray 3Di. No documented capacity constraints in 2025, but systems are ordered 6-9 months in advance for major fabs.

nodes.name: Wafer-to-wafer (W2W) bonding and alignment systems (hybrid bonding, permanent bonding)
nodes.description: Precision wafer-bonding systems for hybrid bonding (copper-dielectric pad bonding at <350°C) and permanent bonding. Sub-50nm alignment accuracy required for fine-pitch interconnects. Vendors: EVG (SmartView alignment, ~26% market share), SUSS MicroTec (~21%), BESI (leaders in hybrid bonding), Applied Materials, Canon, ASMPT. Lead time 12-18 months. Critical for 2.5D/3D interposer and chiplet assembly.

metrics.name: EVG market share (W2W bonding)
metrics.description: EV Group holds leading position in automatic wafer bonding equipment with ~1500+ installed chambers; source: 2025 market analysis.

metrics.name: SUSS MicroTec market share (W2W bonding)
metrics.description: SUSS MicroTec is the second-largest player in wafer bonding equipment; 2024 revenue €446.1M (+46.6% YoY) driven by HBM/advanced packaging.

metrics.name: Alignment accuracy (EVG SmartView)
metrics.description: Industry-leading sub-50nm alignment accuracy achieved by EVG; critical for hybrid bonding fine-pitch (≤5µm pitch) interconnects.

metrics.name: System delivery lead time
metrics.description: Typical 12-16 month lead time from order to installation for W2W bonding systems; sourced from EVG and SUSS product literature.

nodes.notes: W2W bonding is a key enabler for hybrid bonding, which is ramping rapidly for HBM4 and advanced logic packaging. EVG is dominant; BESI specialized in hybrid bonding (>150 cumulative orders, 18 customers). No acute shortage in 2025, but OSAT capacity buildouts are constrained by 12-18 month tool delivery windows. Hybrid bonding revenue at BESI projected to grow from €36M (2023) to €476M (2026).

nodes.name: Thermocompression bonding (TCB) systems for chip-to-substrate and die-to-wafer
nodes.description: Precision thermocompression bonding equipment for micro-bump flip-chip bonding (Cu/Sn solder under 250-280°C, <5 µm placement accuracy). Used for die-attach and chiplet-to-substrate integration. Major vendors: ASMPT (largest installed base, 35-40% market share target by 2027, TAM >$1B), BESI, Kulicke & Soffa (K&S). ASMPT's FIREBIRD TCB delivers ±2µm placement accuracy. Hybrid bonding tool typical cost: $10-20M with 12-18 month lead time.

metrics.name: ASMPT installed base
metrics.description: ASMPT shipped 250th thermocompression bonding tool as of 2025; company holds largest installed base globally and targets 35-40% market share by 2027.

metrics.name: Placement accuracy (ASMPT FIREBIRD)
metrics.description: ±2.0µm placement accuracy for flip-chip bonding; cycle time <2 seconds for high-volume production.

metrics.name: Bonding temperature process window
metrics.description: Thermocompression bonding typically 250-280°C; critical for underfill capillary wetting and solder reflow control.

metrics.name: Tool delivery lead time (estimated)
metrics.description: Bonding tool lead time 12-18 months, mentioned in AMKOR capex disclosure as constraint on 2026 capacity expansion.

nodes.notes: TCB is critical for flip-chip bonding in HBM and advanced AI accelerators. ASMPT dominates with FIREBIRD and NANO Lite platforms (250+ units shipped). BESI competes in hybrid bonding (W2W) but also offers TCB solutions. K&S historically led but ASMPT gained share via process innovation. Market TAM expected to exceed $1B by 2027. Recent orders: ASMPT secured 19 C2S tools for AI packaging (2024-2025). No acute shortage documented, but tool availability is managed through multi-quarter order books.

nodes.name: Underfill dispensing systems (capillary and jet-based)
nodes.description: Automated dispensing equipment for capillary and high-frequency jet underfill (epoxy, flowable-underfill) application between flip-chip die and substrate. Jet systems (Nordson ASYMTEK IntelliJet up to 1.8M dots/hour, 1kHz frequency) enable tight-gap filling for <20µm pitches. Vendors: Nordson ASYMTEK (dominant, non-contact jetting), ITW EAE/Camalot (capillary+jet hybrid), Axxon (Mycronic), GPD Global. Process window critical: void-free fill with minimal solder-bump squeeze-out and fast cycle time.

metrics.name: ASYMTEK IntelliJet frequency
metrics.description: Maximum jetting frequency 1000Hz for ultra-fast underfill fill in tight-pitch geometries; throughput up to 1.8M dots/hour.

metrics.name: Minimum gap fillable (jet)
metrics.description: Modern jet systems can fill gaps <20µm with <5% void rate; critical for fine-pitch bump (<25µm) and chiplet assembly.

metrics.name: Vendor count (mature market)
metrics.description: Nordson ASYMTEK, ITW Camalot, Axxon, GPD Global; established supplier base with multiple capable options.

nodes.notes: Underfill dispensing is a mature, multi-sourced process. Nordson ASYMTEK leads with IntelliJet non-contact jetting technology. ITW Camalot (SmartStream pump) is a strong #2. Equipment cost is moderate (~$0.5-2M) and lead time short (3-6 months). No supply constraints documented. Process innovation focus: improved flowability for void-free fill in narrower gaps and improved thermal conductivity underfill materials (targeting 3-5 W/mK for advanced packages).

nodes.name: Thermal profiling and process control systems (flip-chip, underfill, reflow)
nodes.description: Sensors and software for real-time temperature profiling of flip-chip thermocompression bonding, underfill curing, and reflow soldering processes. Multi-thermocouple probe design with integrated data acquisition and analytics. Vendors: KIC Thermal (specialized for semiconductor packaging, patented sensor hardware), Datapaq (Fluke subsidiary), Speedline, others. Critical for process validation and yield improvement; part of in-line quality control for advanced packaging lines.

metrics.name: Thermal profiling market CAGR
metrics.description: Thermal profiling market projected CAGR 2024-2030; market valued at ~$1.8B by 2030. Source: FutureMarketInsights.

metrics.name: Measurement accuracy (typical)
metrics.description: ±2°C measurement accuracy for multi-thermocouple profilers; critical for process window optimization.

nodes.notes: Thermal profiling is a supporting metrology tool, not a process bottleneck. KIC Thermal is a specialist company serving semiconductor packaging; Datapaq (part of Fluke) serves broader electronics manufacturing. Systems cost $50k-200k and are standard equipment in OSAT advanced packaging lines. No supply constraints.

nodes.name: Wafer probe testing and contactors (fine-pitch bumped die, known-good-die qualification)
nodes.description: Automated probe test systems and custom probe heads/contactors for functional and parametric testing of fine-pitch bumped chiplets (100-650µm pitch). Validates power delivery, signal integrity, memory function (HBM core test), and thermal transient response. Integrated with ATE platforms (Teradyne Magnum 7H for HBM, Cohu-Xcerra-LTX-Credence integrated platform). Spring probe technology for WLCSP compatibility. Critical for known-good-die (KGD) and known-good-interposer (KGI) qualification in chiplet assembly flow.

metrics.name: Teradyne Magnum 7H data rate (HBM)
metrics.description: Supports HBM3/3E test data rates up to 4.5 Gbps; configurable up to 9,216 digital pins + 2,560 power pins.

metrics.name: Probe pitch range (spring technology)
metrics.description: Spring probe systems cover 100µm to 650µm pitch (HYDRA RF, xWave families); enables fine-pitch WLCSP testing.

metrics.name: ATE market leader share (Advantest + Teradyne)
metrics.description: Advantest and Teradyne account for 70%+ of global ATE market; Cohu (including Xcerra, LTX-Credence) is the #3 player.

nodes.notes: Wafer probe testing is a critical quality gate for KGD qualification and HBM stack testing. Teradyne's Magnum 7H platform is industry-standard for HBM base-die and stacked-die testing. Cohu (through Xcerra acquisition) offers integrated ATE + handler solutions with proprietary probe technology (HYDRA RF, xWave). No supply constraints in 2025, but ATE/probe head customization for new HBM variants requires 3-6 month lead time.

nodes.name: Laser dicing (singulation) systems for chiplets and modules
nodes.description: Precision laser dicing systems for wafer singulation post-packaging. DISCO stealth dicing and KABRA processes minimize chipping, mechanical stress, and thermal damage to solder bumps and interconnects. Alternative to mechanical saws for advanced packages. DISCO dominates with 70-80% global share and 4,000+ cumulative unit shipments by 2025. Laser dicing market share grew from 26% (2022) to 31.8% (2025) driven by chiplet/advanced-packaging adoption.

metrics.name: DISCO global market share (dicing equipment)
metrics.description: DISCO Corporation holds 70-80% market share in semiconductor dicing saws; ~4,000 cumulative laser dicing units shipped by 2025.

metrics.name: Laser dicing market share (vs mechanical)
metrics.description: Laser dicing product type held 31.8% market share in 2025, up from 26% in 2022, driven by chiplet/2.5D/3D adoption.

metrics.name: DISCO system cost (estimated)
metrics.description: Typical DISCO laser dicing system cost $2-4M depending on specification; lead time 6-9 months.

nodes.notes: DISCO is a near-monopolist in laser dicing (70-80% share). Company has immense pricing power and sticky relationships with TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix. Stealth dicing pioneered by DISCO is preferred for chiplets to minimize stress and bump damage. No acute shortage in 2025, but capacity is allocated to tier-1 fabs months in advance. DISCO stock (6146.T) is debt-free with 54% ROIC. Laser dicing is a secondary (not primary) bottleneck: it is a downstream singulation step after all assembly and test, so it affects module delivery timeline but not module assembly yield.

nodes.name: Plasma surface activation and cleaning (wafer bonding prep)
nodes.description: Plasma treatment systems for pre-bonding wafer surface preparation (N2/O2 plasma activation, megasonic cleaning). Enables low-temperature bonding by creating reactive surface dangling bonds. Vendors: Keylink Technologies, Nordson MARCH, Finetech (Argon plasma module). Now qualification requirement at leading TSMC, Samsung, Intel fabs. Process time ~10-30 min per wafer lot.

metrics.name: Vendor count (established market)
metrics.description: Keylink Technologies, Nordson MARCH, Finetech are primary established suppliers; multi-sourcing available.

metrics.name: Plasma activation time
metrics.description: Typical N2 plasma activation time 10-30 min per wafer lot; critical for wafer-bonding cycle time.

nodes.notes: Plasma activation is an established, multi-sourced process. Keylink Technologies has supplied systems to leading TSMC/Samsung packaging lines. Nordson MARCH is a diversified supplier. Finetech integrates plasma module into their femto die-bonding platform. No supply constraints documented. Equipment cost moderate (~$0.5-2M) and lead time 6-9 months.

nodes.name: Curing and reflow furnace systems (underfill, encapsulant, solder reflow)
nodes.description: Precision thermal processing ovens for underfill curing, encapsulation, and solder reflow in advanced packaging assembly. Temperature ramp/soak/cool profiles critical for stress management and void elimination. Integrated with thermal profiling systems for process validation. Vendors: Despatch, BTU, Heller, others (traditional SMT equipment suppliers). Cost $0.3-1M, lead time 4-8 months.

metrics.name: Temperature profile ramp rate
metrics.description: Typical ramp rate 3-10°C/min for underfill curing and solder reflow to minimize thermal stress.

metrics.name: Vendor count (established market)
metrics.description: Multiple mature vendors (Despatch, BTU, Heller, etc.) offer standard curing ovens; multi-sourcing available.

nodes.notes: Curing and reflow furnaces are commodity equipment with multiple qualified suppliers. No supply constraints. Equipment is integrated with thermal profiling systems (KIC, Datapaq) for process control and validation.

nodes.name: Environmental test chambers (thermal cycling, burn-in qualification)
nodes.description: Climatic chambers for thermal cycling (-55°C to +125°C) and burn-in testing of packaged modules. Standard JEDEC qualification: AEC-Q100 500-1000 cycles, burn-in at elevated temp/voltage/power. Vendors: multiple (Unitherm, Weiss, others). Typically racked with test handlers (Cohu, Teradyne) and parallel tester cards. Critical gate for reliability qualification of HBM modules and AI accelerators.

metrics.name: Vendor count (established market)
metrics.description: Multiple established chamber suppliers (Unitherm, Weiss, TPS, others); no supply concentration.

metrics.name: Thermal cycling standard
metrics.description: JEDEC AEC-Q100 qualification standard: -55°C to +125°C, 500-1000 cycles, 10-15 min dwell at each extreme.

nodes.notes: Environmental test chambers are commodity equipment. No supply constraints. Multiple qualified suppliers available. Critical for reliability validation but not a production bottleneck—qualification occurs in parallel with high-volume production.

Primary vendor for hybrid-bonding and HBM package inspection alongside Camtek and Onto Innovation. Parent company: Comet Holding (public, SIX: COMET).

nodes.name: Despatch Industries (USA, thermal processing ovens)
nodes.description: US-based manufacturer of precision thermal processing ovens for semiconductor and electronics assembly. Supplies curing and reflow furnaces for underfill, encapsulation, and solder reflow in advanced packaging. Commodity equipment supplier with multi-vendor competition (BTU, Heller, others).
nodes.notes: Despatch is a commodity thermal-processing equipment supplier with low supplier concentration (multi-vendor market). No supply constraints.

nodes.name: Teradyne Inc. (USA, automated test equipment leader)

Serves advanced packaging and AI accelerator module qualification. Publicly listed NASDAQ: TER. #1-2 global ATE market leader (70%+ with Advantest).

edges.claim: Post-assembly X-ray inspection is critical for HBM stack voids, solder defects, and bond-line integrity verification.
Pre-underfill optical bump inspection validates die placement accuracy and solder-bump morphology for chiplet assembly.
Wafer-to-wafer bonding with sub-50nm alignment is essential for interposer-to-substrate integration in 2.5D packages.
Thermocompression bonding enables flip-chip micro-bump attachment with precise placement accuracy and minimal thermal stress.
Underfill dispensing (capillary or jet) follows flip-chip bonding to encapsulate bumps and reduce mechanical stress.
Thermal profiling during bonding and underfill curing validates process window and yield optimization.
Fine-pitch wafer probe testing qualifies known-good die prior to chiplet assembly and system integration.
Laser dicing (DISCO stealth/KABRA) is preferred for chiplet singulation to minimize solder-bump damage.
Plasma surface activation is a pre-bonding requirement for low-temperature hybrid bonding and wafer bonding.
Precision thermal furnaces cure underfill and manage solder-reflow profiles in flip-chip assembly.
Environmental chambers (thermal cycling, burn-in) are essential for JEDEC reliability qualification of HBM modules.
